claims.text: The baseline is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The as-deposited baseline coating has a relatively coarse near-surface grain structure.
Ultrasonic burnishing refines the near-surface grains of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The refined near-surface microstructure has an increased density of grain boundaries.
The increased grain-boundary density facilitates in situ formation of a thin oxide layer during high-temperature sliding.
The oxide layer promoted by the refined microstructure is stable and adherent.
Finer near-surface grains enhance dislocation pinning.
Finer near-surface grains increase surface hardness.
Refined grain boundaries promote rapid and uniform formation of a protective oxide film at high temperature.
The protective oxide film and higher hardness mitigate adhesive wear by limiting plastic flow during sliding.
The protective oxide film and higher hardness mitigate abrasive wear and micro-cracking during sliding.
Burnishing lowers the friction coefficient relative to the untreated coating under high-temperature sliding.
Burnishing reduces the wear rate relative to the untreated coating under high-temperature sliding.
The burnished coating develops fewer and smaller micro-cracks than the untreated coating.
The burnished coating exhibits less localized plastic flow than the untreated coating.
The burnished coating develops a more uniform and adherent oxide layer than the untreated coating.
The predicted effects should hold approximately from 673 K to 1073 K, where oxidation and dynamic-recovery processes are active.
The effects may differ at room temperature or under substantially different sliding loads.
